subject: IB Diploma Physics
name: IB Physics
about: IB Diploma Physics teaching-hour plan. Hours from the IB guide; lesson durations share each topic's hours. Built by lessongen/ib_plan.py.
source: IB Physics guide, first assessment 2025 (understandings numbered here in guide order, SL then AHL).

lessons.title: Describing motion: position, distance and displacement, scalars and vectors
Velocity and acceleration as rates of change; average and instantaneous values
Motion graphs: displacement–time, velocity–time and acceleration–time for uniform and non-uniform acceleration
The equations of motion for uniform acceleration (suvat), including free fall
Projectile motion without air resistance: independent horizontal and vertical components
The effect of fluid resistance on projectiles and falling objects: range, trajectory, time of flight and terminal speed
Newton's three laws of motion and forces as interactions between bodies
Free-body diagrams, resolving forces and finding the resultant force; equilibrium and inclined planes
Types of force: contact forces (normal, friction, tension, elastic, viscous drag, buoyancy) and field forces (gravitational, electric, magnetic)
Linear momentum and its conservation in the absence of a resultant external force
Impulse, force–time graphs and F = Δp/Δt, including systems where mass changes
Elastic and inelastic collisions and explosions: momentum and kinetic energy
Circular motion: angular velocity, centripetal acceleration and centripetal force
Conservation of energy, energy stores and transfers, and Sankey diagrams
Work done by a force: W = Fs cos θ, and the area under force–displacement graphs
Kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy, and their interconversion
Elastic potential energy and energy conservation in systems with springs
Power as the rate of energy transfer, P = Fv, and efficiency
Energy density and specific energy of fuel sources
Torque, rotational equilibrium and the effect of an unbalanced torque
Rotational kinematics: angular displacement, velocity and acceleration, and the rotational equations of motion
Moment of inertia: distribution of mass about an axis, for point masses and standard shapes
Newton's second law for rotation: τ = Iα, with combined linear and rotational systems
Angular momentum, angular impulse and conservation of angular momentum
Rotational kinetic energy and rolling: total kinetic energy of a rolling body
Reference frames, Galilean relativity and Galilean velocity addition
Einstein's two postulates and the Lorentz transformations
Relativistic velocity addition and the invariant spacetime interval
Proper time and proper length, time dilation and length contraction
Relativity of simultaneity and spacetime (Minkowski) diagrams
Muon decay experiments as evidence for time dilation and length contraction
The molecular model of solids, liquids and gases; density; Kelvin and Celsius temperature scales
Temperature and average kinetic energy, internal energy, and the direction of thermal energy transfer
Specific heat capacity, specific latent heat and phase changes at constant temperature
Conduction, convection and thermal radiation; the rate of conduction ΔQ/Δt = kAΔT/Δx
Black-body radiation, the Stefan–Boltzmann law, luminosity and apparent brightness
The black-body spectrum and Wien's displacement law
Energy balance of the Earth: conservation of energy, emissivity and albedo
Variation of albedo, the solar constant and the mean incoming intensity S/4
Greenhouse gases and their sources; absorption of infrared by molecular energy levels
Models of the greenhouse effect: resonance, molecular energy levels and a simple energy-balance calculation
The enhanced greenhouse effect: evidence, feedbacks and responses
Pressure as force per unit area, and amount of substance (the mole and Avogadro constant)
The ideal gas model and the empirical gas laws (Boyle, Charles, Gay-Lussac)
The ideal gas equation PV = nRT = NkT
Kinetic theory: pressure from molecular momentum changes, P = ⅓ρv̄², and molecular speeds
Internal energy of an ideal monatomic gas, and when real gases behave ideally
The first law of thermodynamics Q = ΔU + W, work done by a gas W = PΔV, and ΔU = (3/2)nRΔT
Thermodynamic processes: isovolumetric, isobaric, isothermal and adiabatic; PV^(5/3) = constant
Entropy: a measure of disorder, ΔS = ΔQ/T and S = k_B ln Ω
The second law of thermodynamics, irreversibility and local decreases of entropy
Cyclic gas processes and heat engines; efficiency η = useful work ÷ input energy
The Carnot cycle and the Carnot limit η = 1 − T_c/T_h
Cells as sources of emf, circuit diagrams, electric current I = Δq/Δt and potential difference V = W/q
Conductors and insulators, the origin of resistance, R = V/I and resistivity ρ = RA/L
Ohm's law, ohmic and non-ohmic I–V characteristics, and electrical power P = IV = I²R = V²/R
Series and parallel combinations of resistors and circuit analysis
Emf and internal resistance ε = I(R + r), and variable resistors as rheostats and potential dividers
Conditions for simple harmonic motion and the defining equation a = −ω²x
Describing SHM: period, frequency, angular frequency, amplitude, displacement and their graphs; T = 1/f = 2π/ω
The mass–spring system T = 2π√(m/k), the simple pendulum T = 2π√(l/g), and energy changes in SHM
Phase angle and the SHM equations x = x₀ sin(ωt + φ) and v = ωx₀ cos(ωt + φ)
Velocity as a function of displacement: v = ±ω√(x₀² − x²)
Energy in SHM: E_T = ½mω²x₀², E_p = ½mω²x² and E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²)
Transverse and longitudinal travelling waves; wavelength, frequency, period and v = fλ
The nature of sound waves: compressions, rarefactions, speed in different media and audible range
Electromagnetic waves and the EM spectrum; differences between mechanical and electromagnetic waves
Wavefronts and rays; reflection, refraction and transmission at boundaries
Diffraction around obstacles and through apertures; wavefront–ray diagrams
Snell's law, refractive index, critical angle and total internal reflection
Superposition of waves and pulses, and coherent sources
Interference conditions (path difference nλ and (n + ½)λ) and Young's double-slit experiment s = λD/d
Single-slit diffraction: the intensity pattern and the first minimum θ = λ/b
Single-slit diffraction modulating the double-slit interference pattern
Multiple slits and diffraction gratings: nλ = d sin θ
Applications of diffraction gratings: spectra, spectroscopy and comparing interference arrangements
Formation of standing waves; nodes, antinodes, amplitude and phase along a standing wave
Standing waves on strings: harmonics and the frequencies f = nv/2L
Standing waves in pipes: open and closed ends, harmonics and resonance tubes
Resonance, natural frequency, driving frequency and damping (light, critical, heavy)
The Doppler effect for sound and electromagnetic waves, and wavefront diagrams for moving sources and observers
The Doppler equation for light Δf/f = Δλ/λ ≈ v/c, and red-shift of stars and galaxies
Doppler equation for sound with a moving source: f′ = f v/(v ± u_s)
Doppler equation for sound with a moving observer: f′ = f (v ± u_o)/v, and comparing the two cases
Kepler's three laws of planetary motion
Newton's universal law of gravitation F = Gm₁m₂/r², and treating spherical bodies as point masses
Gravitational field strength g = F/m = GM/r²
Gravitational field lines: radial and uniform fields, and representing combined fields
Gravitational potential energy E_p = −Gm₁m₂/r as work done assembling a system from infinity
Gravitational potential V_g = −GM/r and field strength as the potential gradient g = −ΔV_g/Δr
Work done moving a mass W = mΔV_g, and equipotential surfaces
Escape speed v_esc = √(2GM/r) and orbital speed v_orbit = √(GM/r)
Energy of orbiting satellites: E_k = GMm/2r, E_p = −GMm/r, E_total = −GMm/2r, and changing orbits
Orbital decay: the qualitative effect of a small viscous drag on orbital height and speed
Electric charge: like charges repel, unlike attract; conservation of charge and the elementary charge
Coulomb's law F = kq₁q₂/r², with k = 1/4πε₀
Charging by friction, contact and induction, including grounding
Millikan's oil-drop experiment as evidence for the quantization of charge
Electric field strength E = F/q and electric field lines; field of a point charge
Uniform electric field between parallel plates: E = V/d
Magnetic field lines: bar magnets, straight wires, coils and solenoids
Electric potential energy E_p = kq₁q₂/r as work done assembling charges from infinity
Electric potential V_e = kQ/r as a scalar, zero at infinity
Field strength as potential gradient E = −ΔV_e/Δr, and V–r and E–r graphs
Work done moving a charge W = qΔV_e, and electric equipotential surfaces
Motion of charged particles in uniform electric fields: acceleration and parabolic deflection
The magnetic force on a moving charge F = qvB sin θ and Fleming's left-hand rule
Circular motion of charged particles in uniform magnetic fields: r = mv/qB
Motion in perpendicular electric and magnetic fields: the velocity selector v = E/B
Force on a current-carrying conductor F = BIL sin θ, and force between parallel wires F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/2πr
Magnetic flux Φ = BA cos θ and flux linkage
Faraday's law of induction ε = −NΔΦ/Δt
Motional emf: ε = BvL for a straight conductor moving perpendicular to a field
Lenz's law: the induced current opposes the change producing it, as a consequence of energy conservation
The a.c. generator: sinusoidal emf from a rotating coil, and the effect of rotation frequency
The Geiger–Marsden–Rutherford experiment and the discovery of the nucleus
Nuclear notation ᴬ_Z X: nucleon number, proton number and nuclides
Emission and absorption spectra as evidence for discrete atomic energy levels; photon emission and absorption
Photon energy E = hf = hc/λ and energy level calculations in eV and J
Spectra as evidence of chemical composition: identifying elements in lamps, flames and stars
Nuclear radius R = R₀A^(1/3) and the constant density of nuclear matter
Distance of closest approach and deviations from Rutherford scattering at high energies
The Bohr model of hydrogen: E = −13.6/n² eV and quantized angular momentum mvr = nh/2π
The photoelectric effect as evidence for the particle nature of light, and threshold frequency
Einstein's photoelectric equation E_max = hf − Φ, stopping potential and graphs
Diffraction of particles as evidence for the wave nature of matter, and wave–particle duality
The de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p for particles
Compton scattering as further evidence for the particle nature of light
The Compton shift Δλ = (h/m_e c)(1 − cos θ)
Isotopes, mass defect and nuclear binding energy
Binding energy per nucleon against nucleon number, and mass–energy equivalence E = mc² in nuclear reactions
The strong nuclear force, and the random, spontaneous nature of radioactive decay
Alpha, beta-minus, beta-plus and gamma decay: changes in the nucleus, decay equations and neutrinos
Penetration and ionizing ability of alpha, beta and gamma radiation, and safety
Activity, count rate and half-life; decay over integer half-lives and correcting for background radiation
Evidence for the strong force, the neutron–proton ratio and stability, and constant binding energy per nucleon above A ≈ 60
Discrete nuclear energy levels from alpha and gamma spectra, and the continuous beta spectrum as evidence for the neutrino
The decay law N = N₀e^(−λt), the decay constant, and λ as the probability of decay per unit time
Activity A = λN = λN₀e^(−λt) and the relationship T½ = ln 2/λ
Spontaneous and neutron-induced fission and the energy released
Chain reactions: critical mass, controlled and uncontrolled chain reactions
Nuclear power stations: moderator, control rods, heat exchanger and shielding; fission products and waste management
Stellar equilibrium between radiation pressure and gravity, and fusion as the energy source of stars
Conditions for fusion (high temperature and density), and the effect of stellar mass on evolution
The Hertzsprung–Russell diagram: main sequence, red giants, supergiants and white dwarfs
Stellar parallax: measuring distance d (pc) = 1/p (arcsec)
Determining stellar radii from luminosity and temperature
